exEn: What color is your car?
note: Also means paint: Våt färg! (Wet paint!). After r, the g sounds like j.

exEn: Don't go yet, it's red!
note: Neuter: rött with double t (ett rött äpple, rött vin).

exEn: She has big blue eyes.
note: Neuter: blått. Plural: blå, in speech often blåa.

exEn: The grass is so green after the rain.
The bananas aren't yellow yet.
I drink my coffee black.
note: The neuter stays svart: ett svart hus.

ex: Vi fick en {vit} jul i år.
exEn: We had a white Christmas this year.
note: Neuter: vitt (vitt vin, white wine).

exEn: The sky is so gray today.
note: Neuter: grått. Plural: grå, in speech often gråa.

ex: Jag letar efter ett par {bruna} skor.
exEn: I'm looking for a pair of brown shoes.
note: Also means tanned: Du är så brun! (You are so tanned!)

ex: Min dotter vill bara ha {rosa} kläder.
exEn: My daughter only wants pink clothes.
note: Never changes form: en rosa tröja, ett rosa hus, rosa skor.

exEn: She has dyed her hair purple.
note: The everyday word for purple. Never changes form. Don't mix it up with lilla (little).

ex: På hösten blir löven gula och {orange}.
exEn: In the fall the leaves turn yellow and orange.
note: Stress on the second syllable, ending in the sj-sound. Usually unchanged in form. The fruit is en apelsin.

ex: Vi har köpt en {beige} soffa till vardagsrummet.
exEn: We've bought a beige sofa for the living room.
note: Said like "bäsch", ending in the sj-sound. Never changes form.

exEn: The water was turquoise and warm.
note: Stress on the last syllable. Unlike rosa and lila, it takes endings: turkost, turkosa.

exEn: The ring is made of real gold.
note: For the color, say guldfärgad or i guld: skor i guld. In sports: ta guld (win gold).

exEn: She got a silver bracelet.
note: Definite form: silvret. For the color: silverfärgad (en silverfärgad bil).

ex: Han hade på sig en {ljusblå} skjorta.
exEn: He was wearing a light blue shirt.
note: ljus- (light) and mörk- (dark) go with any color: ljusgrön, mörkröd. Lj- sounds like j.

exEn: The suit is dark blue, not black.
note: Works the same with other colors: mörkgrön, mörkbrun, mörkröd.

exEn: She has long blond hair.
note: Neuter: blont (blont hår). Used about hair and people.

exEn: The children painted colorful pictures.
note: Literally "color-happy". Neuter: färgglatt.

exEn: The cookie is shaped like a heart.
note: Also fitness: i bra form (in good shape). En bakform is a baking tin.

ex: Rita en stor {cirkel} mitt på pappret.
exEn: Draw a big circle in the middle of the paper.
note: C sounds like s. The e drops in the plural: cirklar.

ex: En {kvadrat} har fyra lika långa sidor.
exEn: A square has four sides of equal length.
note: Square meter: kvadratmeter (kvm). A town square is ett torg.

ex: Vår trädgård är en lång, smal {rektangel}.
exEn: Our garden is a long, narrow rectangle.
note: Stress on the second syllable. The e drops in the plural: rektanglar.

exEn: Cut the sandwich into two triangles.
note: Stress on the second syllable. The e drops in the plural: trianglar.

exEn: Write your name on the line.
note: Also a bus or subway line: linje 4. A line of people waiting is en kö.

exEn: The ladybug is red with black spots.
note: No rude meaning in Swedish. På pricken means exactly, spot on.

exEn: What a nice pattern on your sweater!
note: The e drops in the definite: mönstret, mönstren. Plural: mönster (no ending).

exEn: The earth is round.
note: The neuter runt is also the preposition "around": runt hörnet.

exEn: Is the table round or square?
note: Fyr- (four) + kant (edge): covers both squares and rectangles. Figuratively: rigid.

exEn: The road is completely straight here.
note: Rakt fram = straight ahead. Rakt hår = straight hair.

exEn: We have a gray, striped cat.
note: From en rand (a stripe), plural ränder.

ex: Vi satt på en {rutig} filt i parken.
exEn: We sat on a checkered blanket in the park.
note: From en ruta (a square, a box). Rutigt papper = graph paper.

ex: Hon hade en {prickig} klänning på festen.
exEn: She wore a polka-dot dress at the party.
